prompt: Was the founder of the bank that was established 42 years before the National Banking Act was expanded to include the Territory of Hawai'i still alive when it acquired Pioneer Federal Savings Bank?
answer: No. The bank was founded in 1858 as Bishop & Co. by Charles Reed Bishop—42 years before the National Banking Act was extended to the Territory of Hawaiʻi in 1900. Bishop died in 1915, whereas First Hawaiian Bank’s acquisition of Pioneer Federal Savings Bank occurred decades later, so he was not alive at the time of the acquisition.
